newsitem.title: ETHIOPIA: OAU secretary-general Salim congratulates Annan.
newsitem.headline: OAU secretary-general Salim congratulates Annan.

text.p: The secretary-general of the Organisation of African Unity (OAU), seen as a potential candidate for the post of U.N. secretary-general, congratulated Ghanaian Kofi Annan on Saturday on winning the post.

Salim Ahmed Salim of Tanzania said Annan's selection on Friday was a victory for Africa and the OAU, which supported a second term for an African after Washington opposed Egypt's Boutros Boutros-Ghali.

"I am confident that given your vast experience and commitment, you will be able to live up to the enormous challenges and responsibilities that face you as secretary-general," Salim said in a message sent to Annan.
South Africa backed Salim as the next U.N. secretary-general but he was never nominated after President Nelson Mandela said France had threatened to veto him because he speaks no French.
Secretary-general of the OAU since 1989, Salim was a candidate for the U.N. job 15 years ago but the United States vetoed him because of the then Tanzanian government's socialist approach.
